topic: Why Bellamy Was Never Just A Coward
title: One Piece: Bellamy Was Never Just A Coward
description:
Bellamy explained: the Jaya loudmouth everyone writes off as a coward does something very different once you follow him from Mock Town to the Corrida Colosseum. This One Piece breakdown tracks Bellamy through chapters 232, 299, 706, 731 and 744, steelmans the case against him, and shows what his last choice says about him.

Is Bellamy a coward who chases whoever is strongest, or a believer who simply picked the wrong boss? Pick a side in the comments.

comment: Is Bellamy a coward who just follows whoever is strongest, or a loyal believer who picked the wrong boss? Pick one and defend it.

lines.text: Bellamy is not a coward, and chapter 706 is where that label starts to fall apart.

shot.fallback: spring-legged pirate with a fur coat staring down a colosseum crowd

lines.text: Everyone remembers the Jaya punch, the spring legs, and the loud mouth shut in a single hit.

shot.search: Bellamy Luffy punch Jaya Mock Town
shot.fallback: pirate flattened through wooden boardwalks by a rubber fist

lines.text: So why does that same man later walk up to Luffy, face to face, in front of a whole colosseum?

shot.search: Bellamy approaches Luffy Lucy Corrida Colosseum
shot.fallback: pirate walking up to a masked gladiator in an arena

lines.text: I think he may be the most misread character in the whole Dressrosa arc.

shot.fallback: pirate officer candidate in a gladiator arena

lines.text: But how did a label this wrong stick for so long?

shot.fallback: rowdy pirate crew in a rough harbor town

lines.text: I'm following him from Jaya to Dressrosa, with a chapter number on every claim.

shot.fallback: pirate with tears on his face looking down

lines.text: I think it falls apart by the end, so start with the loudest moment of his life...

shot.fallback: arrogant pirate laughing loudly in a town square

lines.text: Bellamy first shows up on Jaya as the loudest pirate in Mock Town, and he wants everyone to know it.

shot.fallback: pirate swaggering through a lawless harbor town

lines.text: His crew, the Bellamy Pirates, treat that town like their own playground.

shot.fallback: group of pirates laughing in a seaside town

lines.text: He eats the Bane Bane no Mi, a Paramecia fruit that turns his limbs into springs.

shot.search: Bellamy Bane Bane no Mi spring legs
shot.fallback: pirate with coiled spring legs bouncing in the air

lines.text: That powers his Spring Hopper attack, which is all bounce and sharp angles.

shot.fallback: pirate bouncing off walls with spring legs

lines.text: Then word gets around that Mont Blanc Cricket has dug up some gold, and Bellamy decides it should be his.

shot.search: Mont Blanc Cricket gold Jaya Bellamy
shot.fallback: old explorer with a golden treasure on a jungle shore

lines.text: Cricket and the Saruyama Alliance are the dreamers of that island, and Bellamy's crew has been laughing at them for it.

shot.fallback: band of cheerful explorers on a rocky coast

lines.text: When he meets Luffy, he laughs at the city of gold, at the sky island, at the whole idea of chasing a dream.

shot.search: Bellamy mocks Luffy Jaya city of gold
shot.fallback: pirate sneering at a boy in a straw hat

lines.text: Here is the detail people forget. He isn't sneering at weakness. He's sneering at plain hope.

shot.fallback: pirate with a cruel grin looking down at someone

lines.text: I read that as his whole creed: dreams are for fools, and fools are who you take from.

shot.fallback: two pirates facing each other on a wooden pier

lines.text: So he springs in to finish it, and in chapter 232 Luffy answers with one downward punch.

shot.fallback: rubber boy driving a single punch down through wooden planks

lines.text: Bellamy goes straight through the boardwalks, and the loudest man on the island is flat.

shot.fallback: pirate lying in a broken wooden walkway

lines.text: The irony is that the dream he laughed at was real, because the city of gold sits high above Jaya in Skypiea, waiting.

shot.fallback: ruined golden city floating among clouds

lines.text: In chapter 299, Cricket hears the golden bell from far below and breaks down in tears, because the city was real all along.

shot.search: Mont Blanc Cricket crying golden bell Jaya
shot.fallback: old explorer weeping happily as a bell rings

lines.text: That's the scene everyone remembers: one hit, one joke, one loud pirate put firmly in his place.

shot.fallback: pirate crashing onto a wooden street

lines.text: But look at what it actually proves. Bellamy misjudges a stronger opponent, and that's arrogance, not cowardice.

shot.fallback: stunned pirate staring up from the ground

lines.text: Cowards avoid fights they can't win. Bellamy walks into one because he's sure he can.

shot.fallback: pirate lunging forward on spring legs

lines.text: So the real question isn't whether he was afraid on Jaya. It's what that loss did to the way he saw strength.

shot.fallback: beaten pirate staring at the sky

lines.text: And the answer is waiting in the boss he stands behind next...

shot.search: Doflamingo Warlord grin pink feather coat
shot.fallback: tall blond man in a pink feather coat grinning

lines.text: Right after Skypiea, Doflamingo shows up for the first time, and he's Bellamy's superior.

shot.fallback: tall man in sunglasses and a feather coat smiling

lines.text: So Bellamy was never a lone wolf. He answered to a Warlord from the start.

shot.fallback: powerful warlord towering over a pirate subordinate

lines.text: That changes how I read the Jaya swagger. A man that loud usually has a bigger name standing behind him.

shot.fallback: pirate bowing before a grinning boss

lines.text: Much later, he turns up again in the Corrida Colosseum on Dressrosa, in B Block.

shot.fallback: pirate stepping into a roaring colosseum

lines.text: His goal is written plainly: win this tournament and become an officer in the Donquixote Pirates.

shot.fallback: pirate saluting a feather-coated boss

lines.text: The crowd even treats him as a popular fighter, which is a strange thing to say about a coward.

shot.fallback: cheering crowd in a stadium watching a pirate

lines.text: To prove his loyalty, he has already handed Doflamingo a gold pillar. Honestly, I find that image very hard to forget.

shot.fallback: pirate presenting a tall golden pillar to his boss

lines.text: Stop and think about that. He lost to Luffy in one punch, and his answer is more loyalty, not less.

shot.fallback: pirate kneeling before a smiling warlord

lines.text: Chapter 706 then gives us my favorite detail. Before the fighting starts, Bellamy recognizes Luffy in his Lucy disguise.

shot.fallback: pirate staring at a masked gladiator in a helmet

lines.text: He walks up to him, says his goal is to join Doflamingo, and says he no longer holds a grudge.

shot.search: Bellamy talks to Luffy Lucy Corrida Colosseum
shot.fallback: pirate speaking calmly to a masked gladiator

lines.text: Then he walks away. As far as the chapter shows, he never exposes the disguise to the arena.

shot.fallback: pirate turning his back and leaving an arena entrance

lines.text: That's a man holding the one card that could ruin Luffy's day, and choosing not to play it.

shot.fallback: pirate keeping a secret while a crowd roars

lines.text: Meanwhile the battle royale begins, and the strategist Dagama forms an alliance that is partly aimed at taking Bellamy out.

shot.search: Dagama alliance Elizabello Tank Lepanto Bellamy
shot.fallback: group of gladiators teaming up against one fighter

lines.text: Think about who gets ganged up on first. Nobody builds an alliance against a coward.

shot.fallback: lone pirate surrounded by gladiators

lines.text: He takes on Tank Lepanto, the former bounty hunters Abdullah and Jeet, and eventually runs into Bartolomeo.

shot.fallback: pirate fighting several gladiators at once

lines.text: Bartolomeo's barrier is brutal. Every time Bellamy attacks, he's the one who takes the damage.

shot.search: Bartolomeo Bellamy Bari Bari barrier fight
shot.fallback: pirate bouncing off an invisible barrier

lines.text: And still he grabs hold of Bartolomeo and tells him not to underestimate his power.

shot.fallback: tired pirate gripping an opponent stubbornly

lines.text: That isn't a man who runs. That's a man swinging at a wall because he refuses to stop.

shot.fallback: pirate punching a transparent wall again and again

lines.text: Then Elizabello throws his King Punch, Bartolomeo's barrier holds, and Bellamy gets carried out of the ring.

shot.fallback: giant king throwing a massive punch at a barrier

lines.text: Even then he talks to Luffy, and Bartolomeo overhears him calling the masked man Straw Hat.

shot.fallback: pirate on a stretcher speaking to a masked gladiator

lines.text: That's how Bartolomeo learns who Lucy really is, which matters a lot later.

shot.fallback: green-haired fan stunned with wide eyes

lines.text: But the real test of Bellamy isn't the tournament. It's what his own side does to him next...

shot.fallback: pirate watching a small fighter approach with a cruel smile

lines.text: Doflamingo's side offers Bellamy a second chance at officer status, and the price is taking Luffy down.

shot.search: Bellamy second chance officer mission Luffy
shot.fallback: pirate receiving an order from a grinning boss

lines.text: It sounds generous. Read the next scene and it looks more like a trap with his name on it.

shot.fallback: pirate cornered by a small masked fighter

lines.text: Bellamy walks up to Luffy to carry out the mission, and that's when Dellinger steps in.

shot.fallback: small fighter blocking a pirate's path

lines.text: Dellinger announces that Doflamingo expects Bellamy to fail again, so the order is to have him killed.

shot.fallback: small fighter smirking at a stunned pirate

lines.text: I want you to sit on that. The boss sends him on a mission he expects him to lose, then arranges his removal.

shot.fallback: pirate realizing his boss has betrayed him

lines.text: Dellinger beats Bellamy badly in chapter 731, and Bartolomeo steps between them with his barrier.

shot.fallback: green-haired fan shielding a fallen pirate with a barrier

lines.text: Bartolomeo's reasoning is simple. They fought on the same battlefield, so they're friends, and he won't let a friend go down.

shot.fallback: green-haired pirate protecting a tired rival

lines.text: Bellamy's reaction is the line I think about most. He tears up and says he has nothing to live for.

shot.search: Bellamy crying nothing to live for Bartolomeo
shot.fallback: pirate crying with his head bowed

lines.text: He asks Bartolomeo why he's even bothering. That's the opposite of a man trying to save his own skin.

shot.fallback: pirate being carried by a green-haired ally

lines.text: A coward wants to survive. Bellamy, at his lowest point, says he doesn't care if he does.

shot.fallback: defeated pirate with lowered eyes

lines.text: So the break in him isn't fear. I read it as grief for the only thing he ever built his life around.

shot.fallback: pirate looking at a tall golden pillar in sorrow

lines.text: And even now he doesn't ask for a place to hide. He says there's no exit, and he wants out to meet Doflamingo.

shot.search: Bellamy Bartolomeo Luffy no exit Colosseum
shot.fallback: three pirates talking in a stone corridor

lines.text: Sabo shows up right then, in chapter 744, and Luffy's whole night changes, but Bellamy's question stays unanswered.

shot.search: Sabo appears Bartolomeo Luffy Bellamy Colosseum
shot.fallback: blond man with a top hat appearing in a corridor

lines.text: But notice what Bellamy has just told us that he wants. Not escape. An answer.

shot.fallback: pirate with a hard stare toward a distant palace

lines.text: And he gets that answer on a palace roof, from the very man who sent Dellinger after him...

shot.fallback: feather-coated warlord on a palace rooftop

lines.text: On that roof, Bellamy finally finds Doflamingo and demands to know why Dellinger was sent after him.

shot.fallback: tired pirate facing a tall warlord on a roof

lines.text: Take a second with that. He walks up, alone and hurt, to the Warlord who just ordered him gone.

shot.fallback: lone injured pirate walking toward a grinning boss

lines.text: Doflamingo doesn't flinch. He says the two of them always had different goals, and takes Bellamy down.

shot.fallback: feather-coated warlord striking a pirate with strings

lines.text: That's it. No speech, no apology. The man who received a gold pillar answers with one cold line and a blow.

shot.fallback: warlord looking down coldly at a fallen pirate

lines.text: Luffy arrives mid-scene and gets furious at what Doflamingo did.

shot.fallback: rubber boy furious with clenched fists

lines.text: He charges, and Doflamingo grabs Bellamy and uses him as a human shield.

shot.fallback: warlord holding a pirate in front of himself

lines.text: Then he takes control of Bellamy with his strings and forces him to attack Luffy.

shot.fallback: puppet-like pirate controlled by glowing strings

lines.text: Here's what I think is the most important beat in Bellamy's whole story. Luffy refuses to hit him.

shot.fallback: straw-hat boy lowering his fist before a puppeted pirate

lines.text: He turns away from the puppet and charges at Law instead, and even his enemies are confused.

shot.fallback: rubber boy running past a puppeted pirate

lines.text: Think back to Jaya. There, Luffy puts Bellamy through a boardwalk for mocking dreams.

shot.fallback: pirate thrown through wooden planks

lines.text: Here, he won't lift a hand against him. Same Luffy, same Bellamy, opposite call.

shot.fallback: straw-hat boy standing before a controlled pirate

lines.text: Luffy didn't suddenly forgive a coward. He saw a man who'd been used, and he judged him differently.

shot.search: Luffy sees Bellamy used by Doflamingo
shot.fallback: determined boy looking at a pirate trapped by strings

lines.text: From what I can find, the fight ends with Luffy putting Bellamy on the ground.

shot.search: Luffy knocks down Bellamy Doflamingo strings
shot.fallback: rubber boy driving a pirate into the ground

lines.text: It's the same fist as Jaya, opposite meaning. On Jaya it ends a mocker. In Dressrosa it ends a puppet show.

shot.fallback: fist stopping a puppet's strings

lines.text: So if Bellamy isn't a coward, why does everyone still call him one? That's the best argument against me...

shot.fallback: pirate with an uncertain expression

lines.text: Here's the strongest case that he is a coward, and I'll give it full weight.

shot.fallback: pirate lowering his head before a boss

lines.text: He bows to a stronger boss, brings a gold pillar to earn a place, and chases an officer's title.

shot.search: Bellamy gold pillar Donquixote Family officer
shot.fallback: pirate carrying a golden pillar toward a throne

lines.text: After Jaya, he doesn't question the creed that humiliated him. He just changes which strong man he serves.

shot.fallback: pirate standing behind a smiling warlord

lines.text: That's a man who attaches himself to power, and I won't pretend that part isn't true.

shot.fallback: pirate beside a towering feather-coated figure

lines.text: But notice the word we keep using. Attaching to power is ambition, even ugliness. It isn't the same thing as fear.

shot.fallback: pirate lost in thought in a dim hall

lines.text: Fear is when you protect yourself. Everything Bellamy does in Dressrosa costs him something.

shot.fallback: bruised pirate gritting his teeth

lines.text: He takes a beating from Bartolomeo's barrier, a worse one from Dellinger, and the worst of all from his own boss.

shot.fallback: battered pirate sitting among rubble

lines.text: A coward in his seat has an easy shortcut: sell out Luffy's disguise to earn the promotion.

shot.fallback: pirate eyeing a masked gladiator thoughtfully

lines.text: Bellamy has that shortcut in chapter 706, and as far as we can see, he walks right past it.

shot.search: Bellamy Luffy no enmity Corrida Colosseum
shot.fallback: pirate turning away from a masked gladiator

lines.text: My read is that people mix up two flaws. Bellamy has terrible judgment about who deserves his loyalty.

shot.fallback: pirate staring at a smiling boss who turned on him

lines.text: He doesn't have bad nerve. The Jaya punch is just the loudest moment, so it becomes the whole story.

shot.fallback: pirate crashing through wooden boards

lines.text: That's the first half of my verdict. The ending of his story proves it, and it's the quietest scene he gets...

shot.fallback: pirate standing apart from a cheering crew on a shore

lines.text: After Dressrosa, the Straw Hat Grand Fleet launches, and Bellamy is there to see it.

shot.search: Straw Hat Grand Fleet launch Dressrosa
shot.fallback: fleet of pirate ships sailing out together

lines.text: He refuses to pledge himself as Luffy's subordinate. Read that twice: the beaten man turns Luffy down.

shot.fallback: pirate shaking his head before a straw-hat captain

lines.text: But he does take a piece of Luffy's Vivre Card, as a precaution for the day he might need it.

shot.fallback: pirate holding a small torn piece of paper

lines.text: That's the most Bellamy decision in the series. He won't be anyone's underling again, and he won't burn the bridge either.

shot.search: Bellamy Luffy Vivre Card Dressrosa end
shot.fallback: pirate tucking a paper scrap into his coat

lines.text: I read that as the first choice of his that has nothing to do with who is strongest.

shot.fallback: pirate smiling faintly in the sunlight

lines.text: On Jaya he judged people by strength. In Dressrosa he learned that strength didn't protect him from his own boss.

shot.fallback: pirate looking back at a distant island

lines.text: So he picks a third option: no master, but an open line to the man who refused to hit him.

shot.fallback: two pirates standing together without speaking

lines.text: Later, a short story in the manga about the Grand Fleet shows him leaving piracy to apprentice as a dyer.

shot.search: Bellamy dyer apprentice Grand Fleet story
shot.fallback: former pirate dyeing cloth in a workshop

lines.text: I love that. The loud man who laughed at dreams ends up learning an honest trade.

shot.fallback: former pirate smiling beside colorful dyed fabric

lines.text: So here's my verdict. Bellamy was never a coward. He was a believer who picked the wrong church.

shot.fallback: pirate standing tall with a steady gaze

lines.text: He believed strength was the only argument, and two things broke that belief: a punch on Jaya and a refusal in Dressrosa.

shot.fallback: split image of a punch and a lowered fist

lines.text: If Oda ever brings him back, that Vivre Card piece is the loaded detail, and I'd bet he shows up rather than hiding.

shot.fallback: pirate watching a paper scrap curl toward the horizon

lines.text: If you want what Doflamingo hid behind those strings, his Holy Knight clue is the next story.

shot.search: Doflamingo Holy Knight clue Mary Geoise
shot.fallback: warlord in a feather coat before a holy city

self_check.hook: Line 1 names Bellamy, states the not-a-coward claim, and cites chapter 706; line 3 asks the core question.
